html:
Kumarajiva was a Buddhist monk from Kucha, an oasis kingdom on the Silk Road, who became the greatest translator of Buddhist texts into Chinese. Many of his translations are still the ones read today.

His father was an Indian noble and his mother a princess of Kucha. As a boy he studied in Kashmir and Kashgar and turned to Mahayana Buddhism, especially the philosophy of Nagarjuna. His fame spread to China.

In 384 a Chinese general captured Kucha and took him east. He was held in the northwest for some seventeen years. In 401 the ruler of the Later Qin brought him to Chang'an, gave him honours and a team of hundreds of monks, and he spent his last years translating.

  • the Lotus Sutra
  • the Diamond Sutra
  • the Vimalakirti Sutra
  • key works of the Madhyamaka school

Earlier translations were stiff or borrowed Daoist words. His were clear and readable, and they shaped how East Asian Buddhism thought and spoke. He came at the height of Buddhism's spread into China. His statue stands before the Kizil Caves near his home.
